limits: Finite synchronous Intl/Temporal fixtures with explicit en-US/UTC/fixed inputs. API presence alone does not establish equivalent behavior.
Unsupported and incompatible-result rows retain reasons and have no timing samples; they are not speedups.
Rust backends and Node run in separate processes. Each result aggregates independent process medians; raw child batches are retained.

Fresh includes unique-comment source allocation, construction/builtins, evaluation and release. Rust napi-vm includes explicit guest cycle GC; Node releases context references and host GC runs outside batches.
Warm source preserves napi-vm source caches and uses each engine source API; warm call retains a guest function. Nested tiers are not guaranteed identical.
Assertions run outside batch timers; numeric result conversion and result summation are timed. Five warmups, no CPU isolation and no universal runtime score.
The configured rquickjs build has no required Intl/Temporal constructors; it receives no timing or speed ratio for those cases.
Intl.DisplayNames returns US instead of United States in the selected fixture. Its three rows retain the diagnostic and no timing.
Slot/options cloning in bound-method getters is a source-identified candidate, not an attributed explanation of the full runtime gap.
